candidates.attacker_control: Indirect but remote: the JSON written by addInitialFlow contains (a) appConfig.requestURL set from the request URL in JavaScriptBootstrapHandler.createAndInitUI, and (b) the initial UI state produced by the application rendering the request (route/query parameters decoded by the servlet container, or stored user data). An attacker who controls a link to the application can supply percent-encoded '</script>' plus HTML/JS that the container decodes before the application renders it into the initial UIDL; the payload itself need not contain raw '<' in the HTTP request target.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that in the default configuration (isEagerServerLoad()==false) addInitialFlow only writes the CSRF token, which cannot contain '<' (UUID) - so the issue is limited to deployments with the initial UIDL enabled; checked that Jsoup escapes attributes (<base href>, dev-mode gizmo) so those sinks are not vulnerable; checked that the {{APP_ID}} substitution is sanitized to [a-zA-Z0-9]; checked the V14 bootstrap path does escape '<' but only for the initial UIDL string, not for {{CONFIG_JSON}} (appConfig for the main bootstrap path carries no request-derived values other than relative 'contextRoot'), so that path is not equivalently exploitable; checked ServerRpcHandler/UIDL CSRF handling, ElementListenerMap/MapSync DisabledUpdateMode and inactive-node checks, and RouteNotFoundError (Jsoup.clean) and found them properly guarded, so this is not a duplicate of those.
candidates.impact: Reflected/stored cross-site scripting in the application's origin for deployments using the V15+ bootstrap with eager server load: attacker JavaScript can act with the victim's session (read/modify UI state, issue client-callable/RPC actions, exfiltrate page data). Because the injected JSON is inside the bootstrapping script, it also breaks application startup (DoS) even without a full XSS payload.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) The V15+ (client-side) bootstrap is used and the initial UIDL is included in index.html, i.e. DeploymentConfiguration.isEagerServerLoad()/vaadin.initialUidl=true (BootstrapInitialPredicate -> VaadinService.getBootstrapInitialPredicate, default false but commonly enabled for server-side routing of this era). 2) An application view reflects attacker-influenced text into the initial UI state (a standard pattern). 3) The serializer leaves '<' unescaped (see unverified).
candidates.root_cause: IndexHtmlRequestHandler.addInitialFlow() serializes the initial JSON (which contains the initial UIDL, i.e. arbitrary server-side UI state, plus appConfig including requestURL) with JsonUtil.stringify() and appends it raw into a Jsoup DataNode inside a <script> element. JsonUtil.stringify only escapes JSON/JS string metacharacters, so a '<' in any string value can form '</script>' (or '<!--') and terminate the raw-text script element. The equivalent legacy path, BootstrapHandler.BootstrapPageBuilder.getBootstrapJS(), applies initialUIDLString.replace("<", "\\x3C") with a comment explaining precisely these two problems, and JavaScriptBootstrapHandler/IndexHtmlRequestHandler's newer code path omits that neutralization. UiDL string values can originate from request data that the servlet container URL-decodes (path/route parameters and query parameters reflected by the application's views), so an encoded payload such as %3C%2Fscript%3E%3Cscript%3E... becomes '</script><script>...' inside the JSON.
candidates.title: Initial UIDL/app-config JSON embedded unescaped into index.html <script> (client-side bootstrap), enabling script-block breakout/XSS
candidates.trace: Request -> VaadinServlet/IndexHtmlRequestHandler.synchronizedHandleRequest (line 65) -> BootstrapInitialPredicate.includeInitialUidl true -> includeInitialUidl() -> getInitialJson() -> createAndInitUI(JavaScriptBootstrapUI) adds appConfig.requestURL and getInitialUidl(ui) returns UidlWriter.createUidl(ui,...) containing UI state -> addInitialFlow() builds 'window.Vaadin = {TypeScript: ' + JsonUtil.stringify(initialJson) + '};' and appends it as a DataNode to a new <script> element inserted at head position 0 -> indexDocument.html() writes the DataNode raw -> browser terminates the script at the injected '</script>' and parses the following attacker HTML/JS in the application origin. Contrast: the same initial UIDL written by BootstrapHandler.getBootstrapJS() is neutralized via replace("<", "\\x3C") before being substituted into {{INITIAL_UIDL}}.
candidates.unverified: Could not verify (a) that elemental.json's JsonUtil.stringify really leaves '<' unescaped - the in-repo comment/escaping in BootstrapHandler is the evidence, but the library is an external dependency not present in the snapshot; (b) that the initial UIDL is present in index.html in the target deployment (depends on eagerServerLoad/vaadin.initialUidl and on whether the app renders request-derived text before the first client round-trip); (c) servlet-container decoding behaviour assumed from spec/implementation knowledge (getPathInfo/getParameterMap decode %3C/%2F, raw '<' in the request target is typically rejected). No runtime verification was performed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 / CWE-116 (improper neutralization of '<' when embedding JSON in HTML script context)

coverage_summary: Inspected the flow-server request-handling core (VaadinService/VaadinServlet/VaadinSession, BootstrapHandler + BootstrapUtils, JavaScriptBootstrapHandler, IndexHtmlRequestHandler, WebComponentBootstrapHandler/WebComponentProvider, UidlRequestHandler/UidlWriter/ServerRpcHandler and all rpc/* handlers, StreamRequestHandler/StreamReceiverHandler/StreamResourceRegistry/AbstractStreamResource, StaticFileServer/ResponseWriter, DevModeHandler, Pwa/PwaIcon, PushHandler/PushRequestHandler, Connect controller/access checker/name checker and Spring config, router internals and error views), the flow-data RendererUtil, flow-push resources, and parts of the GWT client and TypeScript frontend (Flow.ts, FlowBootstrap.js, Authentication.ts, Connect.ts, SimpleElementBindingStrategy, ElementListenerMap/ElementPropertyMap, SystemErrorHandler). The P1 relation index was used only for navigation; per get_relation_scope it is partial (671 files parsed, 2 omitted, no control/data-flow or semantic resolution, Spring enforcement unverified) and its 'security_call'/'input' entries are name-based hints, so no area was treated as reviewed merely because the index had no record there. Unit tests under src/test are not present in this snapshot, so no test-based cross-checking was possible.
limitations: The elemental.json library (com.vaadin.external.gwt:gwt-elemental) is an external dependency not present in the snapshot; its string escaping behaviour for '<' could only be inferred from Flow's own workaround/comment in BootstrapHandler (lines 1035-1044).

Whether the initial UIDL is embedded in index.html depends on DeploymentConfiguration.isEagerServerLoad()/vaadin.initialUidl (default false), so the candidate applies to deployments with that flag enabled; this could not be verified for the evaluated deployment.
Servlet-container behaviour (decoding of %3C/%2F in path/query, rejection of raw '<') was assumed from general knowledge; no container configuration or runtime was inspected.
Unit/integration test sources are absent from the snapshot, so behaviour could not be confirmed against tests, and no code was executed (no runtime confirmation of any finding).

P1 index coverage is partial (671/1700 files parsed; no data-flow/control-flow; Spring annotation handling and DI/runtime enforcement unverified), so some attacker-input -> sink chains may be missing from this review.
Large client-side artifacts (GWT-compiled/bundled JS such as vaadinPush.js, atmosphere.js, workbox) were only spot-checked, not fully audited.

rejected_leads.lead: WebComponentBootstrapHandler.getServiceUrl()/modifyPath() trust the request parameter 'url' and use it as the application's SERVICE_URL and as the base for rewritten src attributes in generated JavaScript (flow-server/.../communication/WebComponentBootstrapHandler.java:419-434, 347-363, 260-300).
rejected_leads.reason: Real attacker-controlled parameter without validation, but no convincing exploitation path could be substantiated from source: the src-rewriting path passes values through URI.create(), which rejects quote/illegal-URI characters used for JS-string breakout, and the appConfig JSON is JSON-escaped; the only party that normally sets 'url' is the embedding page itself (WebComponentProvider generates '?url='+bootstrapAddress from the script's own src), so there is no cross-user victim path. Kept as unconfirmed hardening lead only.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultArchiveExtractor.extractZipArchive() extracts zip entries without the canonical-path containment check that the tar branch performs (flow-server/.../frontend/installer/DefaultArchiveExtractor.java:79-96 vs 122-152) - a Zip Slip pattern.
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine asymmetry and CWE-22 pattern, but the archive is the Node.js distribution downloaded from https://nodejs.org (or a developer-configured node.download.root) during a build/dev-time install, not an attacker-supplied input in the runtime threat model; no attacker-controlled path to a malicious archive was evidenced.

rejected_leads.lead: FrontendUtils.getStatsFromExternalUrl() builds a server-side URL from the request 'host' and 'scheme' headers and fetches it (flow-server/.../frontend/FrontendUtils.java:545-601).
rejected_leads.reason: Looks like SSRF/URL injection but is gated behind the non-default isStatsExternal() configuration ('vaadin.externalStatsFile'), the response is only parsed for assetsByChunkName, and no clear confidentiality or integrity impact could be established from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: Unbounded UIDL body read in ServerRpcHandler.getMessage() (StringBuilder loop) - potential memory-exhaustion DoS.
rejected_leads.reason: Container request-size limits and servlet-level protections exist, no size cap is enforced by the framework, but no source evidence of exploitable impact beyond ordinary request handling; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: ResponseWriter.writeRangeContents(): Long.parseLong on attacker-controlled Range values can throw NumberFormatException (500), and 'bytes=0-,0-' makes end-start+1 overflow, producing an empty/incorrect 206 part (flow-server/.../internal/ResponseWriter.java:182-300).
rejected_leads.reason: Both are robustness/availability defects with no disclosure or injection impact identified; the overflow leads to fewer bytes written, not to file-content leakage.

summary: Reviewed the Vaadin Flow snapshot (Flow 6.0-SNAPSHOT, ~1702 files) with emphasis on server-side request handling: bootstrap handlers (BootstrapHandler, JavaScriptBootstrapHandler, IndexHtmlRequestHandler, WebComponentBootstrapHandler/Provider), UIDL/RPC path (UidlRequestHandler, ServerRpcHandler, EventRpc/MapSync/PublishedServerEventHandler handlers, Stream receivers/resources, StaticFileServer/ResponseWriter), router/error views, Connect endpoints and their access checker, plus client GWT/TS bootstrapping code. One lead stands out for a source-evidenced missing defense: the client-side (V15+) bootstrap path embeds the initial UIDL/app-config JSON into a <script> element in index.html without escaping `<`, whereas the sibling V14 bootstrap path explicitly escapes `<` for exactly this reason. Other suspicious spots (web-component `url` parameter trust, Zip Slip in the Node archive extractor, Host-header-based stats fetch, Range-header parsing) are weaker/unconfirmed and are listed as rejected leads.
